summary_paragraph: A female patient with a complex history including systemic lupus erythematosus, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, antiphospholipid syndrome, and prior transplant failure was admitted for hypertensive urgency with vision changes and low-grade fevers. She presented with a blood pressure of 201/112 and reported transient visual disturbances described as flashing colored lights, which resolved in the emergency department. Imaging showed no acute intracranial process. Her hypertension was managed by increasing lisinopril to 40mg daily and adding hydralazine 25mg four times daily. Fevers persisted initially but cultures from blood, urine, and peritoneal fluid were negative for infection. Genital herpes was diagnosed and treated with acyclovir. She remained afebrile by discharge, with stable blood pressure and no complications. She was discharged home with medication adjustments and follow-up plans.
